original_question: Classify all 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere of E^{n+2}. In particular, classify the 3-dimensional 2-type hypersurfaces of S^4 contained in E^5.
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, Problem 3: the open problem asking to study and classify 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere of E^{n+2}, with special emphasis on the 3-dimensional case in E^5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact topic, the ambient Euclidean setting E^{n+2}, and the paper’s highlighted special case in E^5. It is very close to the official formulation of Problem 3 in Section 3.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
missing_details: The draft is not fully stand-alone because it does not define “2-type.” In the paper’s preliminaries, this means that the Euclidean position vector x of the immersion has a spectral decomposition x = c + x1 + x2, where x1 and x2 are nonconstant and satisfy Δx_i = λ_i x_i for two distinct eigenvalues λ1 ≠ λ2; here Δ is the Laplacian of the induced metric on M. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

The paper’s general setup is an immersion of a connected manifold into Euclidean space, so connectedness and immersion are implicit hypotheses missing from the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
Your special case fixes the unit sphere S^4 ⊂ E^5, whereas the paper states the problem for a hypersphere in E^5 more generally. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

No compactness assumption should be inserted: the surrounding discussion explicitly references both compact and local/noncompact results, and Problem 3 itself is stated without compactness. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

The sharp nearby reformulation is omitted: the paper states that every 2-type hypersurface of a hypersphere is mass-symmetric and hence has nonzero constant mean curvature and constant scalar curvature, and conversely that hypersurfaces with nonzero constant mean curvature in the ambient hypersphere and constant scalar curvature are 2-type unless they are open portions of small hyperspheres. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
refined_question: Let M^n be a connected immersed hypersurface of a hypersphere S^{n+1}(r) ⊂ E^{n+2}, and let x:M → E^{n+2} denote its Euclidean position vector. Classify all such M for which x is of Chen 2-type, i.e. x = c + x1 + x2 with x1, x2 nonconstant and Δx_i = λ_i x_i for two distinct real eigenvalues λ1 ≠ λ2 of the Laplacian Δ of the induced metric on M. In particular, classify all 3-dimensional Chen 2-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere S^4(r) ⊂ E^5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, classify all connected immersed hypersurfaces M^n ⊂ S^{n+1}(r) ⊂ E^{n+2} that are not open portions of small hyperspheres and have nonzero constant mean curvature in S^{n+1}(r) together with constant scalar curvature; in particular, do this in the 3-dimensional case inside E^5. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
justification: The draft matches Section 3.1, Problem 3 rather than a broader neighboring problem: it asks specifically about spherical 2-type hypersurfaces and singles out the 3-dimensional E^5 case. Section 1 supplies the hidden definitions needed to make the question self-contained, especially the spectral definition of k-type and the role of the Laplacian on the induced metric. The paragraph immediately preceding Problem 3 gives the paper’s sharpest nearby reformulation in terms of nonzero constant mean curvature and constant scalar curvature, excluding small hyperspheres. The rewrite therefore stays as close as possible to the paper’s actual intent while making the question mathematically stand-alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
